title: Practice with friends
hookLine: a walking friend, a reading friend: in the desert, Arsenius fled people and Antony said our life is with our neighbor
tomorrow: Ananda said good friends are half the path. what did the Buddha say?

lines: A CLUB AT DAWN, OR EARBUDS ALONE.
cards: A running club at dawn, or a solo run with earbuds in and no one to wait for: runners split on it, and each side swears by theirs. The desert monks of Egypt had the same split, about God.
A man named Arsenius had lived at the palace. Tradition says he prayed: Lord, lead me to be saved. And a voice answered: Arsenius, flee from people.
So he did. He ran from everyone, even the brothers who loved him.

teach.h: VIEW ONE: FLEE, BE SILENT, PRAY.
teach.b: View one. The sayings of the desert elders remember a second word Arsenius heard: flee, be silent, pray. Once a monk named Mark asked him straight out: why do you avoid us?
Arsenius said: God knows I love you.

teach.h: I CANNOT BE WITH GOD AND WITH PEOPLE.
teach.b: But I cannot be with God and with people at the same time. That's the best case for solitude. Not coldness.
A man who knew that, for him, company drowned out the voice he'd come to hear. View two.

teach.h: VIEW TWO: OUR LIFE IS WITH OUR NEIGHBOR.
teach.b: Antony, the old father of the desert monks, put it the other way: our life and our death is with our neighbor. If we gain our brother, we have gained God. For Antony, the neighbor isn't a distraction from God.
The neighbor is where you meet God, or fail to. And the tradition didn't pick a winner.
Both sayings sit in the same collection. Christian monks went on living both ways: hermits alone in cells, and brothers in communities.
Even the hermits walked to an elder to ask for a word, and a brother would come knocking. So the desert's answer to practice with friends isn't always, and it isn't never.
It's knowing which kind of monk you are this season, and keeping at least one friend in it.

how: Christian monastic life has long held both hermits and communities. People on many paths keep a walking friend, a reading partner or a small group that meets to practice together.

o: a group retreat run by a teacher, with everyone silent
sharing one piece of your practice with a friend, like a walk
doing your practice alone, then telling friends about it

games.q: the desert elders: tap the pairs.
p: our life and our death is with our neighbor
asked: why do you avoid us?

s: the desert monks all agreed that real practice happens alone
Arsenius fled people, but Antony said our life and our death is with our neighbor.
Arsenius told the brothers he loved them, but couldn't be with God and people at once
that was his answer when a monk asked why he avoided them.
Antony taught that gaining your brother is gaining God
if we gain our brother, he said, we have gained God.

games.q: a friend says she keeps her practice private because people distract her. what's the best case for her side, as the desert kept it?
o: like Arsenius, some need distance to hear God at all, and can love people from there.
she's just shy; every desert monk said practice belongs in a group.
solitude is selfish, and the desert elders threw it out.
games.why: Arsenius said he loved the brothers but couldn't be with God and with people at once. The tradition kept his saying right beside Antony's.

practice: Bring to mind one person who might share one piece of your practice: a walk, a reading, a quiet coffee. Write the invitation as a one-line text, and if it feels right, send it after the sit.
For the rest of the sit, hold their face in mind and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Practice with friends: a walking friend, a reading friend, someone in it with you, the way even the desert hermits had a brother at the door.

carryVoice: Your line: a friend in it. Arsenius fled, Antony stayed, and the desert kept both. See you tomorrow.
